scope: readonly early-validation contract research; no new implementation or test fixture generated
observed_public_route: BatchTimerAssertions.cs UseExecute(context.SetTimeProvider(custom)) after normal bus start; actual size and virtual-clock expiry verified with long-capable ITimer.
unsafe_inferences: No DI TimeProvider does not imply every future batch uses System.
DI TimeProvider registered does not by itself select ConsumeContext batch provider in reviewed common paths.
Endpoint default/System at build time does not preclude later middleware context override.
Custom ITimer long support does not exempt CTS(TimeSpan,TimeProvider) constructor upper range.

possible_contracts.choice: Keep context-selected provider semantics and precreation guard
possible_contracts.does_not_supply: Universal before-receiver-startup guarantee; original F030 closure needs explicit contract decision.

possible_contracts.choice: Declare effective batch provider/timer capabilities early with defined override rules
possible_contracts.preserves: Potential long-capable timers with startup validation
possible_contracts.requires: Production API/ownership contract, capability validation and adversarial normal/custom/override tests; not merely inspecting a default.

possible_contracts.choice: Restrict all batch TimeLimit to System range at startup
possible_contracts.breaks: Proved existing supported custom-long route; requires explicit compatibility decision.

discriminating_future_routes: Invalid System default must fail before a receive transport startup signal, with structured Batch.TimeLimit + bus/endpoint owner and no timer/admission.
Long-capable declared custom provider must start and produce exact size/expiry result and terminal ownership counts.
Late middleware custom provider with no DI provider must have explicit accepted/rejected contract; existing positive case must not disappear silently.
Registered DI custom provider without ConsumeContext override must prove actual selected batch provider, not infer it from registration.
Named buses with identical endpoint names must prove final diagnostic bus identity.
